response_text: In a 2013–2014 national health survey, the share of U.S. children aged 8–17 with elevated blood pressure was estimated at about 0.5% of non-Hispanic white, 2.0% of non-Hispanic Black, 0.9% of non-Hispanic Asian, and 2.5% of Hispanic children. The Black and Asian figures were based on too few children to be reliable and would not be published, though the corresponding shares with normal or borderline blood pressure were precise enough to report.
